question: Interpret the statistical data of this table.
answer:
The chart shows the changes in inbound and outbound quantities over time. From the chart, it can be seen that the inbound and outbound quantities fluctuate over the given period. Each point represents an inbound or outbound event on a specific date. Note that due to the small data sample (only three data points), it provides only a rough visual representation. In real life, we can expect more data points to obtain a more accurate trend chart.
- If there are more data points (e.g., data over several months or years), other types of charts (such as bar charts, stacked charts, or area charts) can be used to more clearly represent inventory trends.

This visualization provides a good starting point for in-depth analysis, such as identifying seasonal changes in inventory levels, predicting future inventory needs, etc. If sufficient historical and relevant data are provided, these analyses may involve more advanced statistical methods or predictive models.
